```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCR-010"
UO = "ufdf"
UO_TITLE = "Ultrafiltration / Diafiltration (Step 10)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (all pulled from config -> model -> outputs) ---
uo_cfg = CFG.unit_op(UO)
p_dv, p_tmp, p_conc = (uo_cfg.param(k) for k in ("diavolumes", "tmp", "final_conc"))
params = report_params(UO)
n_params = len(params)


def rng_str(ab):
    """A parameter range written the way the register writes it."""
    return f"{ab[0]:g}–{ab[1]:g}"


# nominal at-set-point batch (process_summary.csv) — the step's own performance
_ps = csv("process_summary.csv")
_r10 = _ps[_ps.step == uo_cfg.step].iloc[0]
step_yield_10 = float(_r10.step_yield)
ds_mass_g = float(_r10.product_mass_g)
ds_mass_kg = ds_mass_g / 1000.0
ds_conc = float(_r10.ds_concentration_g_per_l)
ds_volume_l = ds_mass_g / ds_conc            # the mass balance the step closes
dna_per_dose = float(_r10.residual_dna_ng_per_dose)
harvest_titer = float(_ps[_ps.step == 3].iloc[0].titer_g_per_l)
conc_fold = ds_conc / harvest_titer
cum_yield_10 = float(yield_waterfall_df().iloc[-1]["Cumulative yield (%)"]) / 100.0

# drug substance attributes measured on the pool this step delivers
DS_KEYS = ["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"]


def capval(key, col):
    return float(cap.loc[cap.key == key, col].iloc[0])


def cqa_lim(key, side="acc_high"):
    return float(cqa_reg.loc[cqa_reg.key == key, side].iloc[0])


agg_mean, agg_max, agg_cpk = (capval("aggregates_hmw", c) for c in ("mean", "max", "Cpk"))
acid_mean, acid_max, acid_cpk = (capval("acidic_variants", c) for c in ("mean", "max", "Cpk"))
dna_max, dna_cpk = capval("residual_dna", "max"), capval("residual_dna", "Cpk")
agg_lim, acid_lim, dna_lim = (cqa_lim(k) for k in DS_KEYS)
agg_margin = agg_lim - agg_mean
acid_margin = acid_lim - acid_mean
_tight = cap.loc[cap.Cpk.idxmin()]
tightest_cqa, tightest_cpk = str(_tight["cqa"]), float(_tight["Cpk"])


# ideal diafiltration washout: residual fraction of a fully permeable solute after N DV
def dv_pct(n):
    return f"{100 * float(np.exp(-n)):.3f}%"


dv_span = float(np.exp(p_dv.prange[1] - p_dv.prange[0]))

# the concentration assay (AMV-3019) expressed at the drug substance target
conc_assay_sd = amv_3019_precision / 100.0 * ds_conc
conc_nor_half = (p_conc.nor[1] - p_conc.nor[0]) / 2.0
conc_par_half = (p_conc.prange[1] - p_conc.prange[0]) / 2.0
conc_nor_sigma = conc_nor_half / conc_assay_sd

# deviation magnitudes, relative to the ranges they sit in
tmp_over_nor = dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi - p_tmp.nor[1]
tmp_under_par = p_tmp.prange[1] - dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi
conc_shortfall = ds_conc - dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l
shortfall_sigma = conc_shortfall / conc_assay_sd
n_dev = len(dev_facts(DOC))

# pre-characterization risk scores RA-001 assigned to this step
ra = ra_scope(UO)
ra_sev, ra_occ, ra_det = (int(ra[c].max()) for c in ("Sev.", "Occ.", "Det."))
ra_rpn = int(ra["Initial RPN"].max())
sev_band, det_band = risk_scale("severity")[ra_sev], risk_scale("detection")[ra_det]
occ_band = risk_scale("occurrence")[ra_occ]

# the tangential flow filtration skid the step is characterized on
_eq = equipment_df().set_index("Equipment").loc["EQ-TFF-142"]
tff_cal_status, tff_cal_due = _eq["Calibration status"], _eq["Next calibration due"]
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Ultrafiltration and diafiltration is the last unit operation of the A-Mab drug substance
process, and it concentrates the virus filtrate, exchanges it into the formulation buffer
and delivers the drug substance at its target concentration. The step forms no critical
quality attribute and is credited with no impurity or virus clearance. The studies reported
here were executed against PCP-010 on a qualified scale-down model of the commercial
tangential flow filtration skid (SOP-1001 and SOP-2013), and their scope was set by the
pre-characterization risk assessment RA-001. This report is the Stage 1 process design
record for the step in the sense used by the process validation lifecycle guidance
[@fda2011], and the development approach behind it is the enhanced approach of ICH Q8 and
ICH Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq11].

The characterization covered `{python} n_params` parameters, which are the number of
diavolumes, the transmembrane pressure and the final drug substance concentration, and all
of them are classified as key process parameters. None is linked to a critical quality
attribute, so the step contributes no element to the design space and no proven acceptable
range is claimed for any of its parameters. At its set-points the step delivered a product
yield of `{python} pct(step_yield_10)` and `{python} f"{ds_mass_kg:.1f}"` kg of drug
substance at `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L, which closes the train at a cumulative product
yield of `{python} pct(cum_yield_10)`.

The drug substance attributes measured on the pool this step delivers meet their acceptance
criteria at commercial scale. Across `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` simulated batches,
with every process parameter of every step drawn about its set-point at one sixth of its
normal operating range, aggregate reached at most `{python} f"{agg_max:g}"` % HMW against a
limit of `{python} f"{agg_lim:g}"` %, and acidic charge variants reached at most
`{python} f"{acid_max:.1f}"` % against a limit of `{python} f"{acid_lim:g}"` %. Acidic
charge variants carry the tightest capability of the three attributes confirmed here, at a
Cpk of `{python} f"{acid_cpk:.2f}"`. The tightest capability of the drug substance as a whole
belongs to `{python} tightest_cqa`, at a Cpk of `{python} f"{tightest_cpk:.2f}"`, and it is
credited to anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration (PCR-008 and PCR-009), which
are the two steps that clear parvovirus.

Execution recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations, both of which were investigated and impact
assessed, both of which were dispositioned as retained, and neither of which changed a
parameter range, a classification or a conclusion of this report (§13). The step delivers
the drug substance at its target concentration and, by the diavolume count set in §4.1, in
the formulation buffer, within the ranges given in @tbl-params and on the scale-down model
described in §3.1. Residual load buffer was not assayed, and the completeness of the
exchange is taken from the washout relation given in §4.1. The step assures no critical
quality attribute on its own, and its outcome rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose principal mechanism of action is
antibody dependent cellular cytotoxicity. The drug substance process runs from the
production bioreactor through harvest and clarification, Protein A capture, low pH viral
inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration to this
step, which is the formulation operation of that train. It takes the virus filtrate, brings
it to the drug substance concentration and buffer, and hands the material on for storage and
fill.

The operation is a tangential flow filtration process, in which the retentate is
recirculated across a membrane whose nominal cut off retains the antibody while
the permeate carries the small solutes (buffer salts, excipients and residual process
chemicals) to waste. It runs in three phases.
The load is first concentrated, then diafiltered against the formulation buffer for a set
number of diavolumes, then concentrated a second time to the target and recovered from the
skid with a buffer flush.

Each of the three parameters acts through a different physical mechanism. The number of
diavolumes sets how completely the load buffer is replaced by the formulation buffer, while
transmembrane pressure sets the permeate flux and with it both the processing time and the
shear the product sees at the membrane surface. The final concentration sets the
concentration of the drug substance and the viscosity at which the pool is recovered. The
product leaves the step at `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L, which is about
`{python} f"{conc_fold:.0f}"` times the titre of the harvested culture fluid.

No critical quality attribute is formed at this step and none is cleared. The glycan, charge
variant and aggregate attributes are established in the production bioreactor (PCR-003), and
host cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A are cleared by the chromatography steps
(PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). Viral safety rests on low pH inactivation, anion exchange and
small virus retentive filtration (PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009). Some clearance
of small solutes occurs across any membrane operation, but it is not predictable and no claim
is made for it, so the impurity levels entering this step are taken to carry through unchanged
to the drug substance.

## Objectives

The study was designed to meet the objectives listed below.

- (i) Confirm that the step delivers drug substance at its target concentration and closes
  the product mass balance for the batch.
- (ii) Establish a normal operating range and a wider characterization range for each of the
  parameters that govern the operation.
- (iii) Confirm that the drug substance quality attributes measured after the step remain
  within their acceptance criteria.
- (iv) Classify each parameter under the decision logic of SOP-4001, and record the evidence
  the classification rests on.
- (v) Provide the ranges and the controls that the Stage 2 process performance qualification
  will be run against.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The characterization follows the lifecycle approach to process validation [@fda2011], and
this report is the Stage 1 record for the step, so the ranges it establishes are the ranges
Stage 2 qualifies. Development follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8 and ICH Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq11], in which process understanding and quality risk management together
decide what is controlled and how tightly [@ichq9]. Criticality is treated as a continuum
and not as a binary label, which is the convention used throughout the A-Mab case study
[@amab2009].

ICH Q5A governs the evaluation of viral safety [@ichq5a], and it is named here only to
record that this step contributes nothing to the viral clearance claim for the drug
substance. The modular clearance argument is built in PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009 and is
consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Related documents

The documents this report depends on, and the document it rolls up into, are listed in

acceptance criteria before any data existed, while the controlled procedures and the

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior product knowledge

Formulation by tangential flow filtration is a platform operation at Novacyte Biologics, and
the same membrane chemistry, the same formulation buffer and the same membrane loading have
been used for three earlier humanized IgG1 products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and throughout
A-Mab clinical supply. That history is why the step is characterized against a known
mechanism instead of developed from first principles. The mechanism is also simple enough to
state in advance, since a membrane that retains the antibody and passes small solutes changes
the composition of the pool and leaves the product alone. The expected outcome of the study
was therefore an absence of effects on product quality.

Two mechanisms could break that expectation, and both were carried into the study. Shear at
the membrane surface can generate aggregate, and transmembrane pressure is the parameter that
governs it. Holding the antibody at high concentration through the second concentration phase
can do the same, and the final concentration is the parameter that governs that. RA-001
scored both as low risk on the platform history recorded there, but they are nevertheless the
reason the characterization ranges were set wider than the normal operating ranges.

## Quality attributes in scope

Three drug substance attributes are measured on the pool this step delivers, and they are the
attributes in scope for this report (@tbl-cqa). None of them is set at this step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(DS_KEYS))
print()
```

: Drug substance quality attributes measured after the step. {#tbl-cqa}

Aggregate is the attribute with a mechanism at this step. It is formed in the production
bioreactor (PCR-003) and reduced principally at cation exchange (PCR-007), and the
concentration and recirculation applied here are the last opportunity in the process to add
to it. Acidic charge variants are formed in the bioreactor and are challenged by the low pH
hold (PCR-006), and they are measured again here because the drug substance is the material
the specification applies to. Residual DNA is cleared across the three chromatography steps
and is reported for the drug substance on a per dose basis, and that conversion of basis is
made at this step.

The remaining attributes of the register are not repeated here. The glycan attributes, host
cell protein and leached Protein A are covered by the reports for the steps that set or clear
them, and the full register with those attributions is given in Appendix C.

## Risk based prioritization and parameter selection

RA-001 carried `{python} n_params` parameters into the pre-characterization assessment for
this step and assigned all of them to univariate study. The scoring is reproduced in
@tbl-risk.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(ra_scope(UO))
print()
```

: Pre-characterization risk ranking and study assignment for the step (RA-001). {#tbl-risk}

The three parameters scored alike, and the reason is visible in the effect column, where none
of the failure modes reaches a quality attribute. Severity was scored in the
`{python} sev_band` band, which the A-Mab scale uses for an unlikely impact on product
quality that calls for no supplemental testing and no reprocessing. Occurrence was scored in
the `{python} occ_band` band and detection in the `{python} det_band` band, and the detection
band is the one the scale uses for a failure that is seen at a later operation and not during
this one. The three scores together give an initial risk priority number of
`{python} f"{ra_rpn:g}"` for each parameter. On that basis
the assessment concluded that a designed experiment was not justified and that univariate
study of each range would support the operating limits the step needs.

A low score is not the same as no study. The parameters still set the concentration and the
buffer the drug substance is delivered in, and both of those are specified, so what the score
decided was the kind of study and not whether one was needed.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

The studies were executed on a scale-down tangential flow filtration system qualified as a
model of the commercial skid under SOP-1001. The model holds the scale independent variables
of the operation at their commercial values. Those variables are the membrane chemistry and
nominal cut off, the membrane loading in product mass per unit area, the crossflow per unit
area, the transmembrane pressure, the number of diavolumes and the final concentration. The
scale dependent features were set to match commercial performance instead of commercial
geometry, which for this operation means the recirculation loop, the pump and the system
hold-up volume.

Qualification compared the model with commercial equivalent runs on the quantities that leave
the step, which are step yield, final concentration, aggregate and charge variants. The
qualification record is held under SOP-1001 and is not reproduced here. The skid used for the
studies (EQ-TFF-142) was `{python} tff_cal_status`, and its next calibration fell due on
`{python} tff_cal_due`.

One feature of the model cannot be matched to the commercial skid by scaling, and it is the
hold-up volume of the recirculation loop and the membrane housing, because buffer held there
is recovered with the pool at the flush and dilutes it. The effect is managed by the recovery
flush described in §3.2, and it is the mechanism behind DEV-010-02 (§13.2).

The warrant this model has to carry is narrow. It supports operating ranges for parameters
that govern process performance, and it supports the statement that the drug substance
attributes are unchanged across the step, but it is not asked to support a quality attribute
claim of its own, because the step makes none.

## Operation

The step was operated as described in SOP-2013, taking as its load the pool from small virus
retentive filtration. That pool is concentrated, diafiltered against the formulation buffer
for `{python} f"{p_dv.setpoint:g}"` diavolumes, then concentrated to
`{python} f"{p_conc.setpoint:g}"` g/L and recovered from the skid with a buffer flush.
Transmembrane pressure is held at `{python} f"{p_tmp.setpoint:g}"` psi through both
concentration phases and through the diafiltration.

Inputs to the step are controlled to platform specification and were not characterized, and
they are the membrane, the formulation buffer and the load itself, whose quality is the
subject of PCR-009. The membrane is installed, flushed and integrity tested before use under
SOP-2013. The system is cleaned and sanitized between batches under the same procedure.

## Analytical methods

The controlled procedures and the validated analytical methods used at this step are listed
in @tbl-refs.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=UFDF_SOP_REFS, amvs=UFDF_AMV_REFS))
print()
```

: Controlled procedures and validated analytical methods for the step. {#tbl-refs}

Protein concentration is measured by ultraviolet absorbance under AMV-3019, and it is both
the quantity that defines the endpoint of the second concentration phase and a drug substance
release test. Aggregate is measured by size exclusion chromatography under AMV-3011 and
charge variants by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing under AMV-3013, and both of these
are release tests applied to the final pool of the step. The values this report gives for
aggregate and for charge variants are the commercial scale estimates of §8, and no result
from an individual run is reported for either. Validated performance for the concentration
method is given in Appendix A. Performance for the other two methods is held in their own
validation reports.

## Sampling plan

Samples were taken at three points of the operation, which were the load before the first
concentration phase, the retentate at the end of the diafiltration, and the final pool after
the recovery flush. The final pool is the drug substance, and it is the sample the release
panel is applied to. Transmembrane pressure was recorded continuously by the skid through both
concentration phases and the diafiltration, which is how the excursion in §13.1 was detected.
Retained samples of the load and of the final pool were kept. No result from a retained sample
is reported here.

## Statistical methods

No designed experiment was run at this step, and none was planned, so the screening and
response surface framework used at the six steps that carry designed experiments does not
apply here. A screening design identifies which factors are active on a quality attribute,
and a response surface model is the predictive model from which a design space is then read.
Both of them need a quality attribute to model. This step governs none, and the analysis is
therefore descriptive.

Two quantitative sources support the statements made in this report. The first is the seeded
nominal batch, run with every parameter of every step at its set-point, which gives the step
performance in @tbl-perf. The second is a Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` commercial scale batches in which every parameter of
every step is drawn independently from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a
standard deviation of one sixth of its normal operating range, and clipped to its
characterization range. The drug substance attributes from that simulation give the
capability reported in §8.

Capability is reported as a one-sided index against the upper acceptance limit of each of the
three attributes, so Cpk is the distance from the simulated mean to that limit expressed in
units of three standard deviations. Aggregate and residual DNA are impurities, and an upper
limit is the whole of their acceptance criterion. Acidic charge variants are shown in @tbl-cqa
with a lower figure as well, and that figure is not the limit capability is taken against
here, because the risk the attribute carries at the drug substance is an elevated level. No
acceptance threshold for Cpk is adopted in this report, and the values are reported against
the acceptance limits themselves, which are the criteria the drug substance is released
against.

# Study design

## Parameters, ranges and the knowledge space

The three parameters, their set-points, their normal operating ranges and their
characterization ranges are given in @tbl-params.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(report_params(UO))
print()
```

: Parameters characterized at the step, with the final classification. {#tbl-params}

Each range was set from the mechanism the parameter acts through. Diafiltration removes a
fully permeable solute exponentially, so the residual fraction of the load buffer after N
diavolumes is e raised to the power minus N. At the set-point of
`{python} f"{p_dv.setpoint:g}"` diavolumes that residual is `{python} dv_pct(p_dv.setpoint)`
of the load concentration. At the low edge of the characterization range it is
`{python} dv_pct(p_dv.prange[0])` and at the high edge `{python} dv_pct(p_dv.prange[1])`,
which is a span of about `{python} f"{dv_span:.0f}"`-fold in carry-over. The range covers a
wide swing in the completeness of the exchange while leaving the exchanged species at trace
level throughout it. This is a design calculation for an ideal, fully permeable solute in a
well mixed retentate, and it is the basis of the range and not a measured result.

Transmembrane pressure was ranged asymmetrically about its set-point, over
`{python} rng_str(p_tmp.prange)` psi against a normal operating range of
`{python} rng_str(p_tmp.nor)` psi. The mechanism that moves transmembrane pressure during a
batch is membrane fouling, and fouling moves it upward, so the characterization range was
extended on the high side only. The excursion recorded in §13.1 reached
`{python} f"{dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi:g}"` psi and therefore fell inside characterized
territory.

The final concentration was ranged `{python} f"{conc_par_half:g}"` g/L either side of the
target of `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L, with a normal operating range half that wide, and
the width of the normal operating range is set by the measurement that controls the endpoint.
Intermediate precision of the concentration method is
`{python} f"{amv_3019_precision:g}"` %RSD (AMV-3019), which at the target is
`{python} f"{conc_assay_sd:.1f}"` g/L, so the normal operating range is about
`{python} f"{conc_nor_sigma:.1f}"` assay standard deviations wide on each side. A range that
is narrow relative to the assay controlling it cannot be held, and this range is not narrow on
that measure.

## Univariate assessment

The characterization schedule took each parameter to both edges of its characterization range
with the other two held at their set-points, and the set-point condition was the reference,
with the levels given in @tbl-levels.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(univariate_levels(UO))
print()
```

: Univariate evaluation levels for the three parameters. {#tbl-levels}

Each level was judged on process performance and not on product quality, and the criteria are
listed in §5.2. Product quality was assessed on the pool of the set-point batch and on the
commercial scale simulation described in §3.5, and not at the edges of the ranges, which is a
boundary §5.4 and §7 carry forward.

A multivariate design was neither run nor needed. Interactions matter when two parameters act
on the same quality attribute, and no parameter of this step is linked to one in the register,
so there is no governed attribute on which an interaction could be estimated or classified.
The two parameters that carry a mechanism at all, which are transmembrane pressure through
shear and the final concentration through the concentrated hold (§2.1), were both scored low
risk in RA-001 on the platform history recorded there. The three parameters also act through
different mechanisms and are read out on different responses, and that is the second reason a
factorial design would have added cost without adding process understanding. Diavolumes are
read out on the composition of the pool, transmembrane pressure on flux and processing time,
and the final concentration on the endpoint of the second concentration phase.

The absence of a quality linkage is a property of the attribute register and not a gap in the
study, and it is what keeps all three parameters out of the design space and inside the
control strategy, where they are held because monitoring them is what keeps the process
consistent [@amab2009].

# Results

## Nominal batch performance and mass balance

The step delivered drug substance at its target concentration and closed the product mass
balance for the batch. The nominal batch is given in @tbl-perf.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(step_performance(uo_cfg.step), floatfmt=",g")
print()
```

: Nominal batch performance of the step at its set-points. {#tbl-perf}

Product loss across the step was `{python} pct(1 - step_yield_10)` of the mass entering it,
and the platform attributes it to hold-up volume and to retention on the membrane. Hold-up
volume is the mechanism behind DEV-010-02 (§13.2), and membrane retention was not measured
separately. The step delivered
`{python} f"{ds_mass_kg:.1f}"` kg of drug substance at `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L, which is
`{python} f"{ds_volume_l:.0f}"` L of pool. Cumulative product yield for the train closes at
`{python} pct(cum_yield_10)`, and the step by step figures are given in Appendix B. Residual
DNA is reported for the drug substance at `{python} f"{dna_per_dose:g}"` ng/dose against a
limit of `{python} f"{dna_lim:g}"` ng/dose.

![Cumulative product yield across the drug substance train, from the production bioreactor to
the formulation step.](../outputs/figures/fig_yield_waterfall.png){#fig-yield width=100%}

The shape of @fig-yield is the reason the step is reported at all, because it costs product
without changing quality, and the loss it costs is of the same order as the losses at the
chromatography steps. It therefore belongs in the mass balance argument even though it
belongs in no quality argument.

## Characterization levels and process performance

The univariate levels of @tbl-levels were assessed against process performance criteria only,
and no product quality result is reported at any of them. The criteria were the permeate flux
and the processing time the level produced, the concentration the second phase reached at its
endpoint, and closure of the product mass balance at recovery. None of those is a quality
criterion, and none of them could be, because no attribute of the drug substance register is
set or cleared at this step.

The quantitative basis of this report is the two sources named in §3.5. The set-point batch
gives the performance of the step, and the commercial scale simulation gives the quality of
the pool it delivers. What the levels add is the width of the region the step was operated
over, which is the region the characterization ranges in @tbl-params describe, and the
limitation that leaves is stated in §5.4 and carried into the classification in §9.

## Drug substance concentration and its measurement

The final concentration is the only parameter of this step that is measured on the product
itself, which makes it both the easiest to demonstrate control of and the easiest to correct.
Intermediate precision of the method is `{python} f"{amv_3019_precision:g}"` %RSD, with a
limit of quantitation of `{python} f"{amv_3019_loq:g}"` g/L and accuracy of
`{python} f"{amv_3019_accuracy:g}"` % (AMV-3019, Appendix A). The method accounts for
`{python} pct(amv_3019_var_frac)` of the observed variance in the reported concentration, so
most of the spread seen between batches is process and not assay.

One run finished its second concentration phase below target, at
`{python} f"{dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l:g}"` g/L, and the shortfall of
`{python} f"{conc_shortfall:g}"` g/L is `{python} f"{shortfall_sigma:.1f}"` times the
intermediate precision of the assay at the target, so it is a real difference and not a
measurement artefact. The pool was corrected in process, and the investigation is reported in
§13.2.

## Product quality across the step

The drug substance attributes measured after the step meet their acceptance criteria, and the
quantitative outcome is given in §8. Aggregate (SEC-HPLC, AMV-3011) is the attribute with a
mechanism at this step, because the product is concentrated and recirculated across a
membrane. Charge variants and residual DNA have no mechanism here at all, and they are
measured on the pool because the drug substance is the material their specifications apply
to.

The quality confirmation covers the normal operating ranges of the three parameters, which is
the region the simulated batches concentrate in. It does not extend to the edges of the
characterization ranges, where the evidence from this study is process performance only, and
that boundary is carried into the range statements in §6 and §7.

# Design space

This step contributes no element to the design space of the A-Mab drug substance process. A
design space is the multivariate combination of parameters that has been shown to assure
quality [@ichq8], and the assurance has to be assurance of something. None of the three
parameters characterized here is linked to a critical quality attribute, so there is nothing
at this step for a design space to assure.

What the step has instead is an operating range for each parameter. The normal operating
ranges in @tbl-params sit inside the wider characterization ranges, and the characterization
ranges are the knowledge space for the step, so operation anywhere inside a normal operating
range is normal operation. Operation outside a characterization range is a change, and it is
assessed under the pharmaceutical quality system before it is made [@ichq10].

The corner of the characterized region that challenges the step hardest is the combination of
the low diavolume edge, the high transmembrane pressure edge and the high concentration edge.
It gives the least complete buffer exchange, the highest shear at the membrane and the highest
product concentration at the same time. That corner is bounded by the range edges in
@tbl-params, and it is a process performance worst case and not a quality worst case, because
no quality attribute is at stake at this step.

These statements are bounded in three ways. They hold over the ranges in @tbl-params and not
beyond them. They rest on the scale-down model described in §3.1, whose warrant is process
performance and unchanged quality and not a quality claim of its own. They assume the membrane
chemistry, the membrane loading and the formulation buffer used in the study, none of which
was varied.

# Proven acceptable ranges

No proven acceptable range is claimed for any parameter of this step. A proven acceptable
range is the range of a parameter over which a named quality attribute stays inside its
acceptance criterion, where the range is proven by supporting data, and that definition needs
a governed attribute, which this step does not have.

What the study supports instead is the operating range in @tbl-params, and its acceptance
basis is process performance. The criteria the ranges were judged against are the target
concentration of the drug substance and closure of the product mass balance, and both of those
are process criteria and not quality criteria. Buffer exchange was not judged against a
measured criterion at all, because it is controlled by the diavolume count, and the residual
load buffer follows from the washout relation given in §4.1.

The proven acceptable ranges that bound the attributes measured after this step are
established elsewhere. Aggregate is bounded at the production bioreactor and at cation
exchange (PCR-003 and PCR-007), charge variants are bounded at the bioreactor and at the low
pH hold (PCR-003 and PCR-006), and residual DNA is bounded across the three chromatography
steps (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). Those reports carry the analysis, and this one carries
the confirmation that the drug substance still meets the criteria after the last operation of
the process.

That confirmation is bounded to the ranges characterized here and to the attributes listed in
@tbl-cqa, and it says nothing about the attributes this step does not measure, which are
covered by the reports named in Appendix C.

# Process capability and robustness

The drug substance attributes measured after this step meet their acceptance criteria at
commercial scale with wide margin, and capability against the upper limit of each is given in
@tbl-cap.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(DS_KEYS))
print()
```

: Commercial-scale capability of the attributes measured after the step. {#tbl-cap}

Aggregate is the most capable of the three, at a Cpk of `{python} f"{agg_cpk:.1f}"`. Its mean
across the simulated batches is `{python} f"{agg_mean:.2f}"` % HMW against a limit of
`{python} f"{agg_lim:g}"` %, a margin of `{python} f"{agg_margin:.2f}"` %, and the highest
simulated batch reached `{python} f"{agg_max:g}"` %. Acidic charge variants carry the tightest capability of the
three, at a Cpk of `{python} f"{acid_cpk:.2f}"`, with a mean of
`{python} f"{acid_mean:.1f}"` % against a limit of `{python} f"{acid_lim:g}"` %, a margin of
`{python} f"{acid_margin:.1f}"` %, and a highest simulated batch of
`{python} f"{acid_max:.1f}"` %. Residual DNA reached at most
`{python} f"{dna_max:g}"` ng/dose against a limit of `{python} f"{dna_lim:g}"` ng/dose, at a
Cpk of `{python} f"{dna_cpk:.1f}"`. Its spread across the simulated batches is smaller than
the rounding @tbl-cap carries, so the deviation column of that row reads zero while its Cpk is
finite.

![Commercial-scale distributions of the glycan attributes, aggregate, host cell protein and
acidic charge variants from the Monte-Carlo simulation, with acceptance limits and the
capability of each panel.](../outputs/figures/fig_capability.png){#fig-capability width=100%}

The simulated distributions are shown in @fig-capability, which plots the glycan attributes,
aggregate, host cell protein and acidic charge variants. Aggregate and acidic charge variants
are the two panels in scope for this report. Residual DNA is not among the panels, and its
capability is given in @tbl-cap. The remaining panels are attributes set or cleared upstream,
and they are covered by the reports named in Appendix C.

The simulation varies every parameter of every step about its set-point, including the three
parameters of this step, on the sampling described in §3.5. The figures therefore already
carry the operating variability this report is responsible for, but they do not isolate it. A
step with no effect on an attribute contributes nothing to the spread of that attribute, which
is why the capability of the drug substance is not by itself a sensitive test of this step.

The tightest capability of the drug substance as a whole is not one of these three. It belongs
to `{python} tightest_cqa`, at a Cpk of `{python} f"{tightest_cpk:.2f}"`, and it is credited
to anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration (PCR-008 and PCR-009), which are the
two steps that clear parvovirus. The low pH hold carries the enveloped virus claim (PCR-006)
and contributes nothing to this one. Capability across every attribute of the drug substance
is consolidated in PCMR-001.

Two bounds apply to all of these figures. They are estimates from qualified scale-down models
under the sampling described in §3.5, and they are not measurements at commercial scale. They
carry the batch to batch variation the model reproduces and not the additional variation a
commercial facility contributes. Capturing the rest is what Stage 2 is for.

# Parameter classification

All `{python} n_params` parameters of this step are classified as key process parameters
under the decision logic of SOP-4001, and none is a critical process parameter or a well
controlled critical process parameter. The classification of each and the reason for it are
given below.

- Number of diavolumes, KPP. It sets the completeness of the buffer exchange, which is a
  formulation property of the drug substance and not a critical quality attribute, and it is
  counted from permeate mass and easy to hold. The characterization range spans a wide swing
  in carry-over, and no attribute of the drug substance register is set or cleared by the
  step, so no quality criterion bounds the range (§2.2 and §5.4).
- Transmembrane pressure, KPP. It governs the permeate flux and the processing time, and
  through shear at the membrane it has the most plausible route of the three to a quality
  effect. It is nevertheless classified on process performance, because this step governs no
  attribute against which such an effect could be classified. It is monitored continuously,
  and the one excursion recorded stayed inside the characterized range (§13.1).
- Final DS concentration, KPP. It is the endpoint of the step and it is measured on the drug
  substance at release, so it is controlled closely for reasons of process consistency and
  not of quality risk. A low result is correctable in process by further concentration, which
  is what happened in DEV-010-02.

Across the whole train `{python} f"{class_counts()['KPP']}"` parameters are classified as key
process parameters, of which `{python} n_params` are at this step. The classification follows
from the quality attribute register, in which no drug substance attribute is set or cleared at
this step, and not from a demonstrated null effect on one. All three parameters stay in the
control strategy because monitoring and controlling them is what keeps the process consistent
and predictable [@amab2009].

# Contribution to the control strategy

The step contributes to the control strategy in four ways, and each of them is a process
performance control rather than a quality control.

The first is parameter control, in which the three parameters are held to the normal
operating ranges in @tbl-params, and those are the ranges Stage 2 will be run against.

The second is in-process monitoring. Transmembrane pressure is trended on the commercial skid
through both concentration phases and the diafiltration, the diavolume count is taken from
permeate mass, and the concentration is measured before the pool is released to storage.

The third is release testing on the drug substance, in which concentration, aggregate and
charge variants are measured on the final pool under AMV-3019, AMV-3011 and AMV-3013, and
those results are the last quality data generated on the batch before it leaves drug
substance manufacture.

The fourth is control of the inputs. The membrane and the formulation buffer are controlled
to platform specification, and a change to either is assessed before it is made, because
neither was varied in this study.

The step also has clear limits. It controls no critical quality attribute, and it provides no
impurity clearance credit and no viral clearance credit. Every attribute in @tbl-cqa is
delivered to it inside its limit by the steps upstream, and the contribution this step makes
is to deliver that material at the right concentration in the right buffer without changing
it. The consolidated control strategy across the train is in PCMR-001.

# Discussion

The step is understood well enough to transfer, and part of the reason is that there is
little to understand, since a membrane that retains the antibody and passes small solutes
changes the buffer and leaves the product alone. The study confirmed that expectation against
the drug substance attributes measured on the pool the step delivers, and it established
ranges for the three parameters that govern how the step performs. Nothing in the result was
unexpected, which is the outcome a platform operation should produce.

Confidence in the scale-down model is high for process performance and adequate for what is
claimed about quality. The model matches the commercial skid on the variables that drive the
operation, and hold-up volume is the one feature it cannot match by scaling. That feature
showed itself during execution as a concentration shortfall on one run (§13.2), and it is
managed by the recovery flush and not by a parameter range.

Two deviations were recorded, and the more significant of them is the transmembrane pressure
excursion, in which pressure reached `{python} f"{dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi:g}"` psi against an
upper normal operating limit of `{python} f"{p_tmp.nor[1]:g}"` psi. It stayed inside the
characterization range, the parameter governs no quality attribute, and the run was retained.
The second deviation was the concentration shortfall, which was corrected in process, and
neither event changed a range, a classification or a conclusion.

Three limitations bound what this report establishes. The first is the absence of a designed
experiment, which means that interactions between the three parameters are not quantified and
that this study cannot exclude one. The justification for accepting that is the justification
for the univariate design itself, which is that no parameter of the step is linked to a
quality attribute in the register (§4.2). If a future process change gives one of them such a
link, the study type has to be revisited.

The second limitation is that the capability figures in §8 are model estimates and not
measurements at scale, and they are confirmed during Stage 2 on batches made in the
commercial facility with the commercial skid. The third is that the ranges hold for the
membrane chemistry, the membrane loading and the formulation buffer used here. A change to any
of them falls outside the knowledge space of this study, and the platform history that
supports the step does not extend to a membrane the platform has not been run on.

No parameter of this step needed the most stringent form of control. That conclusion follows
from the absence of a quality linkage and not from a demonstration of robustness against a
quality attribute, and it is bounded accordingly.

# Conclusions

The step is characterized and ready for Stage 2. It delivers drug substance at
`{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L with a product yield of `{python} pct(step_yield_10)` at
set-point, closing the train at a cumulative product yield of
`{python} pct(cum_yield_10)`.

All `{python} n_params` parameters are classified as key process parameters and none is
linked to a critical quality attribute, so the step contributes no element to the design
space, and it claims no proven acceptable range, no impurity clearance and no viral
clearance.

The drug substance attributes measured after the step meet their acceptance criteria at
commercial scale, with acidic charge variants (icIEF, AMV-3013) the tightest of the three at
a Cpk of `{python} f"{acid_cpk:.2f}"`. Those estimates come from qualified scale-down models
with every parameter drawn about its set-point at one sixth of its normal operating range, and
they are confirmed at commercial scale during Stage 2.

Both deviations recorded during execution were investigated and retained, and neither changed
a range, a classification or a conclusion. The outcome of this report rolls up into PCMR-001.

# Deviations from the plan

Execution recorded `{python} n_dev` deviations against PCP-010. Both were investigated, both
were impact assessed, and both were dispositioned as retained, with the register given in
@tbl-dev.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
```

: Deviations recorded during execution of the study. {#tbl-dev}

Both deviations were found by the controls the plan put in place, one by the continuous
in-process record of transmembrane pressure and the other by the concentration check at the
end of the step. Neither was found after the fact, and neither required a retrospective
assessment of material that had already moved on.

## DEV-010-01 — Transmembrane pressure excursion above the normal operating range

Transmembrane pressure reached `{python} f"{dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi:g}"` psi during the first
concentration phase, which is `{python} f"{tmp_over_nor:g}"` psi above the upper edge of the
normal operating range of `{python} rng_str(p_tmp.nor)` psi. The excursion was detected as it
happened, on the pressure trend recorded by skid EQ-TFF-142.

The investigation reviewed the pressure and flux records for the run. Pressure rose through
the first concentration phase and returned inside the control range once the diafiltration
began, which is the signature of transient membrane fouling and not of a control failure, and
the root cause was recorded on that basis. The skid was `{python} tff_cal_status`, and no
instrument fault was identified.

The impact assessment rests on two facts. The value reached is
`{python} f"{tmp_under_par:g}"` psi inside the upper edge of the characterization range of
`{python} rng_str(p_tmp.prange)` psi, so the excursion sits inside the region this study
covers rather than outside it. Transmembrane pressure governs no quality attribute at this
step, so there is no quality impact to assess. The run was retained, and no range or
classification was changed.

## DEV-010-02 — Final drug substance concentration below target

The second concentration phase finished at
`{python} f"{dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l:g}"` g/L against a target of
`{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L, a shortfall of `{python} f"{conc_shortfall:g}"` g/L. The value
was inside the normal operating range of `{python} rng_str(p_conc.nor)` g/L but below the
target the batch record specifies, and it is `{python} f"{shortfall_sigma:.1f}"` times the
intermediate precision of the concentration method at the target, so it is not an artefact of
the measurement.

The investigation traced the shortfall to residual hold-up volume. Buffer held in the
recirculation loop and the membrane housing was recovered with the pool at the flush, and it
diluted the pool below the concentration the phase had reached. The root cause is a property of the
system rather than of the parameter, and it is the feature of the scale-down model discussed
in §3.1.

The pool was returned to the skid, concentrated to target and confirmed by the ultraviolet
absorbance method (AMV-3019). That correction is a normal in-process adjustment for this
operation and needs no separate product disposition, because the concentration is measured
directly on the product and the material stayed inside its normal operating range throughout.
The run was retained, and the event is recorded here because a repeat would point at the
flush volume and not at the parameter.
